messages.subject: Analysing Limited Data
messages.body_plain:
Help!

For my thesis I involuntary have a small dataset due to a limited population. I was thinking about analysing this data with the statistical model ANOVA, using non-parametric tests or Bayesian statistics. What do you think works best? Or are there any other methods/models/tests I can use?
Any tip ore suggestion will be highly appreciated!
Thank you in advance.

Sincerely,

Inge van der Borg
Utrecht University

messages.subject: Re: Analysing Limited Data
messages.body_plain:
Inge,

It is difficult to make general recommendations without knowing the specifics of the problem. But traditional nonparametric tests discard information in the data and reduce things like power, so I wouldn't recommend those. Bayesian ANOVA might be helpful because you can supplement your small data with prior substantive knowledge of the topic. I think the BayesFactor package has some ANOVA-specific functionality, which may be helpful.

Ed

> > Thanks for the suggestion, I will look at including related code soon (and crediting your contribution).
> >
> > blavaan currently has a BF() function that does a Bayes factor approximation (labeled "experimental" because it is difficult to find a gold standard for comparison), so I will probably move that to a more general "compare" function. It feels like I should call this function "anova()" to follow R precedent. But maybe that is more confusing than worthwhile.
> >
> > Ed
> >
> > On Sat, Dec 10, 2016 at 11:28 PM, Mauricio Garnier-Villarreal <mauga...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > Hi Ed
> > >
> > > I was looking into having the model comparing using functions from the loo package.
> > >
> > > I made this function to use the compare function, maybe including a function like this in blavaan?
> > >
> > > library(blavaan)
> > > library(loo)
> > >
> > > # Not run:
> > > # The Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
> > > HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
> > >               textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
> > >               speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '
> > >
> > > fit <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
> > >             std.lv <http://std.lv>=T)
> > > summary(fit)
> > >
> > > fit2 <- bcfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
> > >             std.lv <http://std.lv>=T, group="school")
> > > summary(fit2)
> > >
> > >
> > >
> > > compare_blav <- function(f1,f2, digits=3){
> > >
> > >   lls1 <- blavaan:::case_lls(f1@external$runjags, f1@Model,
> > >                              f1@ParTable, f1@SampleStats, f1@Options, f1@Cache,
> > >                              f1@Data)
> > >   lls2 <- blavaan:::case_lls(f2@external$runjags, f2@Model,
> > >                              f2@ParTable, f2@SampleStats, f2@Options, f2@Cache,
> > >                              f2@Data)
> > >
> > >   lo1 <- loo(lls1)
> > >   lo2 <- loo(lls2)
> > >
> > >   wa1 <- waic(lls1)
> > >   wa2 <- waic(lls2)
> > >
> > >   summ_loo <- rbind(f1=round(unlist(lo1[1:6]),digits),
> > >                     f2=round(unlist(lo2[1:6]),digits) )
> > >   summ_waic <- rbind(f1=round(unlist(wa1[1:6]),digits),
> > >                      f2=round(unlist(wa2[1:6]),digits) )
> > >
> > >   diff_loo <- compare(lo1,lo2)
> > >   diff_waic <- compare(wa1,wa2)
> > >
> > >   loo_res <- list(summary=summ_loo,diff=diff_loo)
> > >   waic_res <- list(summary=summ_waic,diff=diff_waic)
> > >
> > >   res_all <- list(loo=loo_res,waic=waic_res)
> > >
> > >   return(res_all)
> > > }
> > >
> > > compare_blav(fit,fit2)
> > >
> > >

messages.subject: Robust mediation analysis
messages.body_plain:
Hi, I need help in syntax... How can I do the model below using a robust alternative (t-distribution)?

model <- ' # direct effect
             Y ~ c*X
           # mediator
             M ~ a*X
             Y ~ b*M
           # indirect effect (a*b)
             ab := a*b
           # total effect
             total := c + (a*b)
         '
fit <- sem(model, data = Data)
summary(fit)

Thanks a lot,

Danilo (Brazil)

messages.subject: Re: Robust mediation analysis
messages.body_plain:
Danilo,

blavaan does not allow you to automatically use a robust model. To do it, you will have to export the JAGS code and modify the code yourself. There is an example of this in the blavaan paper; see Sec 4.4 (it is not the same model as yours, but it should give you the idea):

https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.05604.pdf

Ed
